current_leader.name: Adaptive synthetic-monitor frequency optimizer
current_leader.state_transition: fixed synthetic schedule -> operational risk changes -> reduce eligible cadence/coverage within detection guardrails -> avoid billable runs -> restore cadence when risk rises
current_leader.why_survived: Still the strongest precise surviving vertical because billing is usage-linked, schedule mutation is out-of-path, and savings are measurable. Repeated searches have not established large marginal adaptive savings beyond best static tuning, so monetization confidence is reduced and it is now tied with the broad quota-boundary hypothesis.
current_leader.closest_threat: First-party observability vendors possess telemetry and schedule controls; static tuning may capture most savings.
current_leader.smallest_intervention: Read monitor definitions, periods, locations, run history and risk signals; recommend cadence changes; optionally mutate schedules via authorized provider API; measure avoided runs against best-static baseline.
current_leader.monetization: Per optimized monitor-month or capped share of verified savings incremental to best-static baseline.
current_leader.biggest_unresolved_risk: No strong public evidence that dynamic adaptation creates material recurring savings after static cleanup.
current_leader.next_research_test: Quantify marginal adaptive savings versus best-static using realistic enterprise synthetic estates; kill if increment is small. Search in parallel for a precise vertical exceeding 45/60.
